title: Mosaic Media — inference scaling & cost sweep (POC notes)
content:
Summary:

This document captures the results and operational notes from the Mosaic Media POC performance sweep (June 7–13, 2026). Mosaic’s product team wanted a data-driven recommendation for serving long-context summarization and metadata extraction for live video transcripts (average request size: 3,200 tokens; target response length: 150 tokens). Goals: quantify latency and cost across hosted vs Dedicated deployment profiles, identify scaling knee points, and surface configuration knobs that meet an internal p95 SLA of 700ms for short responses and an aspirational 1.5s p95 for the 150-token summaries for production.

Testbed and inputs:
- Dataset: 2,400 anonymized transcript windows (3k–6k tokens per window) sampled from Mosaic beta. Each request trimmed to a 3,200-token context using sliding-window heuristics.
- Model family: open LLaMA-2-style variant fine-tuned for summarization (13B dense baseline) plus 13B 4-bit (q4f16) quantized variant onboarded for POC.
- Prompt pattern: system + user with tool-calling stub; average prompt overhead 80 tokens. Output target: ~150 tokens.
- Workload types: single-request latency (no batching), small-batch (batch size 4 requests), burst load (concurrent 120 req/s sustained for 2m), and steady-state throughput (concurrent 20 req/s for 30m).
- Hardware: Hosted baseline (n1-standard GPU fleet equivalent), Dedicated testbed using p4d-8x (8x A100 40GB) node pool and gpus with 4 replicas for autoscale experiments.
- Observability: token-level latency traces, KV cache hit metrics, GPU utilization, memory spill events, and cost meter (estimated $/M tokens from infra + hosted per-token rate).

Methodology:
- Each experiment run 3 times; reported median and p95 across runs. Warmup = 300 requests to populate KV caches. For batching experiments we measured end-to-end latency from request arrival to final token emission (streaming disabled for consistent numbers).
- Cost calculation: Dedicated = hourly GPU + infra amortized / observed tokens served. Hosted = Redwood hosted per-token pricing quote used for comparison (as of POC).

Key results (high level):
- Single-request latency (no batching):
  - 13B dense on Dedicated (warm KV): p50 = 210ms, p95 = 550ms (150-token output); p95 dominated by decode compute and memory-copy overheads.
  - 13B q4 on Dedicated: p50 = 190ms, p95 = 470ms; consistent ~15% improvement in p95 vs dense.
  - Hosted baseline (multi-tenant): p50 = 340ms, p95 = 920ms; variability from noisy neighbors and routing fallbacks.

- Small batching (batch=4):
  - Dedicated q4: throughput improves ~3.6x vs single-request; median per-request latency increases ~1.9x, p95 increases ~2.3x. Good tradeoff for absorbable latency budgets.

- Burst (120 req/s for 2m):
  - Dedicated pool with autoscale target=4 replicas: sustained CPU/GPU queueing after 45s; p95 spikes to 2.3s.
  - Increasing auto-scale to target=8 replicas reduced p95 spike to 820ms but doubled infra cost.

- Steady-state (20 req/s for 30m):
  - Dedicated q4 at 4 replicas: stable p95 = 540ms, GPU util ~62%, KV cache hit rate 72%. Cost effective footprint observed.

- Cost estimates (approx, standardized to $ per 1M output tokens):
  - Dedicated q4 (amortized): ~$85 / 1M tokens.
  - Dedicated dense: ~$120 / 1M tokens.
  - Redwood hosted quote (current POC rate): ~$140 / 1M tokens (includes multi-tenant premium and SLA adders).
  - Note: batching and higher KV cache hit rates reduced effective cost by up to 28% in our runs.

Observed bottlenecks and variance drivers:
- KV cache misses for long-context windows: cache warmup strategy matters. Requests with sliding-window shifts >512 tokens drop below 40% hit rate and cause repeated full attention recompute.
- Memory copies during decode path caused non-linear p95 growth at 90%+ GPU utilization. Kernel selection for q4 path was stable but had edge cases with sequence lengths >4k that triggered fallback kernels.
- Networking jitter in hosted routing produced long tails in multi-tenant runs; dedicated deployment eliminated most of these but at fixed infra cost.
- Small-batch packing beneficial, but packing across heterogeneous sequence lengths produces latency outliers; deterministic padding strategy recommended for SLO-critical routes.

Configurational recommendations for Mosaic (short-term POC → prod):
1) Deployment: start with a small Dedicated pool (4x A100-equivalent) running q4 profile for production-critical routes; fall back to Redwood hosted for non-critical, lower-cost development traffic.
2) Autoscale policies: target steady-state with warm KV caches and add headroom of 2 replicas for bursts. Use predictive burst scaling driven by ingress signal from Mosaic CDN.
3) Batching & packing: enable request packing with max-batch=4 for the summarization endpoint; enforce max-seq padding to nearest 64 tokens to reduce padding variance.
4) KV cache strategy: use fixed-size sliding windows with 50% overlap and prefetch on anticipated next-window requests (video segment boundaries) to keep hit rate >70%.
5) Quantization: q4f16 provides favorable p95 and cost; benchmark q8h (8-bit) in a limited run for quality regression before switching.
6) Streaming: enable streaming in prod for perceived latency improvements; retain non-streaming numbers in tests for SLO guardrails.

SLA considerations and recommended SLOs:
- For 150-token summaries: set p95 SLO = 1.2s initially (aligns with Dedicated q4 at 4 replicas).
- For short/high-priority notifications (<50 tokens): set p95 SLO = 550ms using single-request fast-path with cache priming.
- Implement automatic fallback to smaller model (7B fast-tuned) for any sustained p95 > 2s to preserve availability.

Next steps / action items:
- [ACTIONS] Run a 24-hour soak with production-like ingress (mirrored traffic) to validate autoscale thresholds and observe cold-start behavior (owner: Jonah, due: 2026-06-28).
- [ACTIONS] Perf-test q8h quantization on 100 transcript samples for quality/regression (owner: Elena, due: 2026-06-25).
- [ACTIONS] Implement packing + padding enforcement in request router rules and run regression sweep on latency tails (owner: Samir, due: 2026-07-02).
- [ACTIONS] Create a short one-pager for Mosaic GTM summarizing cost tradeoffs and suggested pricing (owner: Aditi, due: 2026-06-30).

Open questions / risks:
- Mosaic expects burst patterns that align with live event boundaries; prediction signal availability from their CDN is TBD. If unavailable, cost to keep headroom increases by ~60%.
- Model quality drift when moving to q4/q8 needs explicit human-eval on domain transcripts; prelim qualitative pass looked acceptable but not comprehensive.
- Regulatory: Mosaic wants optional private deployment in EMEA; we need to validate Dedicated private-network setup and KMS integration timing.

Appendix (raw numbers — median / p95):
- Single-request (Dedicated, q4): median=190ms / p95=470ms (150-token); tokens/sec decode ~210 TPS (output tokens).
- Batch=4 (Dedicated, q4): median/request=360ms / p95=1100ms; aggregate throughput ~680 RPS-equivalent when packed.
- Burst 120r/s (autoscale=4->8): p95 spike observed to 2.3s at 4 replicas -> 820ms at 8 replicas.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally reimbursement-focused (tradeoffs between infra capex and hosted convenience). If Mosaic is price-sensitive and willing to accept slightly larger p95 tails for burst events, we can propose a smaller dedicated footprint + aggressive fallback to hosted on excess load (hybrid router). If low-latency tail is critical for premium customers, we recommend Dedicated + predictive scaling + packing rules as above.

Attachments: linked artifacts include Confluence design doc (CONFLUENCE-3129) and JIRA tasks for packing and q8h runs.

End of POC sweep notes.
